name: Water heater (tank)

combustion.note: Gas and oil models only. A blocked or loose flue spills CO. Standing-pilot controls run on a pilot-flame thermopile (Resideo WT8840); power-vent and electronic-ignition ones need mains power (A.O. Smith GPVT-40, GCF-40 101). kW: burner input of 40 US gal gas tanks, 36,000–50,000 Btu/h (A.O. Smith).

comps.spec: Screw-in heating elements, about 4.5 kW (electric models)
Magnesium anode rod — shavings make a fire starter
comps.loc: Top of the tank, large hex head

comps.spec: Gas control valve with thermocouple (gas models)

notes:
A gas tank with a standing pilot keeps heating water in a power cut: a thermopile in the pilot flame powers the gas control (Resideo WT8840). Gas and oil tanks vent their exhaust through a flue; keep it connected and clear.

Power-vent tanks need mains power: one 40 US gal model is rated 120 V, 5 A, with a 50,000 Btu/h burner (A.O. Smith GPVT-40). So do some tanks that vent up an ordinary flue, such as a 36,000 Btu/h propane model with electronic ignition and a powered flue damper (A.O. Smith GCF-40 101): look for a cord or wiring before counting on hot water in a power cut.
